claims.claim_text: Pieces of this system already exist and prove it works.
claims.evidence_quote: Pieces of this system already exist around the world... several have gone far enough to prove it works.
claims.reasoning: SOURCE asserts existing pieces and that several cases prove it works; identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: No country nears complete transparency, but several prove feasibility.
claims.evidence_quote: No country has achieved anything close to complete transparency, but several have gone far enough to prove it works.
claims.reasoning: Direct paraphrase preserving the concession and the feasibility claim.

claims.claim_text: Sweden's 260-year openness shows transparency endures without collapse.
claims.evidence_quote: Two hundred and sixty years later, Sweden still operates under this principle... The country has not collapsed.
claims.reasoning: 260 years, endurance, and non-collapse are all stated in SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: In 1766 Sweden passed the world's first freedom-of-information law.
claims.evidence_quote: In 1766, Sweden passed the Freedom of the Press Act - the world's first freedom of information law.
claims.reasoning: Date and superlative match SOURCE exactly.

claims.claim_text: It abolished censorship and is now constitutional.
claims.evidence_quote: It abolished censorship... It's now part of the Swedish constitution.
claims.reasoning: Both facts appear verbatim in SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Finnish-Swedish priest-politician Chydenius drove Hats-versus-Caps explicitly anti-corruption law.
claims.evidence_quote: Anders Chydenius, a Finnish-Swedish priest and politician, drove the legislation through parliament. The motivation was explicitly anti-corruption.
claims.reasoning: Name, roles, driving role, and anti-corruption motive all match; Hats/Caps context is adjacent.

claims.claim_text: Offentlighetsprincipen keeps documents public by default 260 years on.
claims.evidence_quote: Two hundred and sixty years later, Sweden still operates under this principle. It's called offentlighetsprincipen... Government documents are public by default.
claims.reasoning: Term, default-public rule, and 260-year persistence all stated.

claims.claim_text: Nordics consistently rank among least corrupt, most effective democracies.
claims.evidence_quote: Nordic countries consistently rank among the least corrupt and most effective democracies in the world.
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim restatement.

claims.claim_text: Seoul's 1999 OPEN system made bribery-prone permitting visible.
claims.evidence_quote: In 1999, Seoul launched the OPEN system... shows citizens exactly who made what decision.
claims.reasoning: Year and the visibility of corruption-prone tasks match.

claims.claim_text: OPEN tracks 70 corruption-prone tasks, including construction, environmental, and urban planning permits, in real time.
claims.evidence_quote: tracks 70 municipal tasks most prone to corruption - construction permits, environmental regulation, urban planning - and shows citizens... in real time.
claims.reasoning: Number 70 is correct, but SOURCE lists environmental regulation and urban planning, not permits, and ties real time to showing citizens.

claims.claim_text: Citizens see exactly who decided what at each process point.
claims.evidence_quote: shows citizens exactly who made what decision, at which point in the process, in real time.
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Previously invisible processing let officials demand speed-up bribes unprovably.
claims.evidence_quote: This opacity enabled bribery: officials could demand payments to "move things along" and nobody could prove it.
claims.reasoning: Opacity-to-bribery causal link and unprovability all stated.

claims.claim_text: Visibility eliminated that bribery leverage entirely.
claims.evidence_quote: Making the process visible eliminated that leverage entirely.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim in meaning.

claims.claim_text: Corruption decreases as e-participation increases; UN, OECD, World Bank recognized it.
claims.evidence_quote: "corruption decreases as e-participation increases." The system was recognized by the UN, OECD, and World Bank.
claims.reasoning: Quote and the three recognizing bodies match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Estonia's 2001 X-Road proves transparency infrastructure scales.
claims.evidence_quote: ### Estonia: The Infrastructure Proof (2001)... If your objection is "this can't scale," look at Estonia's X-Road.
claims.reasoning: Year and scale-proof framing both supported.

claims.claim_text: X-Road links 929+ institutions, 1,887 systems, 3,000+ services, timestamped, signed, logged.
claims.evidence_quote: connecting 929+ institutions, 1,887 information systems, and 3,000+ digital services. Every transaction is timestamped and cryptographically signed. All data access is logged.
claims.reasoning: All three figures and the three properties match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Citizens can see who accessed their data and why.
claims.evidence_quote: Citizens can see who accessed their data and why.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim.

claims.claim_text: Estonia ranks 2nd on the UN E-Government Development Index.
claims.evidence_quote: Estonia now ranks 2nd in the UN E-Government Development Index.
claims.reasoning: Rank and index match.

claims.claim_text: No major breaches in over 20 years despite constant cyber attacks.
claims.evidence_quote: The system has had no major security breaches in over 20 years, despite constant cyber attacks.
claims.reasoning: Negation, duration, and qualifier preserved.

claims.claim_text: X-Road is MIT-licensed open source, deployed in 20+ countries.
claims.evidence_quote: It's open source (MIT license) and deployed in 20+ countries.
claims.reasoning: License and deployment count match.

claims.claim_text: X-Road proves every-email-available infrastructure is technically feasible.
claims.evidence_quote: X-Road proves the "every email available up the chain" infrastructure is technically feasible.
claims.reasoning: Identical claim in SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: The technology is feasible; the bottleneck is will.
claims.evidence_quote: The technology is not the bottleneck. The will is.
claims.reasoning: Meaning preserved.

claims.claim_text: Brazil's 2004 Transparency Portal follows all federal money.
claims.evidence_quote: ### Brazil: Following the Money (2004)... publishes all federal spending.
claims.reasoning: Year heading and all-federal-spending scope match.

claims.claim_text: It publishes contracts, transfers, salaries, travel, and credit-card transactions.
claims.evidence_quote: contracts, transfers, salaries, travel expenses, and government credit card transactions.
claims.reasoning: All five categories match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: The portal receives over 20 million accesses per year.
claims.evidence_quote: It receives over 20 million accesses per year.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim figure.

claims.claim_text: Transparency Card sent 20+ million notifications via 430,000+ active cards.
claims.evidence_quote: over 430,000 active cards, 20+ million notifications sent.
claims.reasoning: Both counts match.

claims.claim_text: Journalists uncovered 60GB of hidden pension payments spanning 27 years.
claims.evidence_quote: they uncovered 60GB of hidden pension payment data going back 27 years.
claims.reasoning: Amount and span match.

claims.claim_text: Give citizens CEO tools and they find the fraud.
claims.evidence_quote: This is what happens when you give citizens the tools to be CEOs: they find the fraud.
claims.reasoning: Restatement preserving meaning.

claims.claim_text: New Zealand publishes cabinet papers by default since 2019.
claims.evidence_quote: Since 2019, New Zealand has proactively published all Cabinet papers and minutes online.
claims.reasoning: Year, actor, and default publishing match.

claims.claim_text: All papers and minutes appear online within 30 business days.
claims.evidence_quote: all Cabinet papers and minutes online within 30 business days of decisions being made.
claims.reasoning: Window and scope match.

claims.claim_text: Cabinet deliberations are typically the world's most protected government information.
claims.evidence_quote: cabinet deliberations are typically the most protected category of government information anywhere in the world.
claims.reasoning: Hedge 'typically' and superlative preserved.

claims.claim_text: Government has not halted; ministers still deliberate; citizens see why.
claims.evidence_quote: The government has not ground to a halt. Ministers have not stopped deliberating. What has changed is that citizens can see why.
claims.reasoning: All three negations and the affirmative claim preserved.

claims.claim_text: Taiwan's vTaiwan crowdsources laws through consensus-finding deliberation.
claims.evidence_quote: Taiwan's vTaiwan platform uses Pol.is to let citizens participate in policy deliberation... surfaces statements that find cross-group consensus.
claims.reasoning: Actor, method, and consensus mechanism match.

claims.claim_text: Pol.is takes agree-disagree votes with no replies, surfacing cross-group consensus.
claims.evidence_quote: vote agree or disagree (no replies allowed - this prevents flame wars), and an algorithm surfaces statements that find cross-group consensus.
claims.reasoning: Voting mode, no-replies rule, and consensus surfacing all present.

claims.claim_text: By 2018, 26 issues processed; 80% led to government action.
claims.evidence_quote: By 2018, 26 issues had been processed, and 80% led to government action.
claims.reasoning: Year, count, and percentage match exactly.

claims.claim_text: Participation is downstream of transparency, not core transparency itself.
claims.evidence_quote: This isn't core transparency - it's what becomes possible downstream of transparency.
claims.reasoning: Negation and downstream framing preserved.
